current.text: At his position he is stuck behind Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson. Nick Claxton is the projected starting center.
The Bulls' 10th rotation spot is open between Patrick Williams, Zach Collins and Miller.
The experts do not see a clear path to regular minutes for him. He may not play over Claxton.
He has played very well in preseason. He also played well late last season.
His preseason shooting is not expected to last.
If Buzelis or Wilson gets hurt, he would likely start and get about 25 minutes.
Draft him only in leagues 180 or more players deep. He is a stash in formats where stashing is easy.
Tiago Splitter is the Bulls' new head coach, replacing Billy Donovan. He is expected to push young players.
Chicago has little depth, so an injury to a main player would open a big role.
Chicago is projected to be a bottom-10 team.

durable.text: He is an active two-way forward who crashes the glass and can play the 3, 4 and 5.
His game should translate well to fantasy if he gets minutes.
Steals are his weakest category. Projections give him very few, well below the top 250 pool.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 362, ESPN rank 308), and the experts only want him in leagues 180 or more deep. That makes him a waiver name in our 144-player draft, not someone to spend on. Keep an eye on him early. If Buzelis or Wilson gets hurt, he could start and get about 25 minutes, and he would be a cheap FAB add with low turnovers and decent efficiency. If he plays only about 14 minutes, there is no reason to roster him.
